The graph of the continuous function $y=f(x)$ is shown above. The points $A$ and $B$ lie on the curve and have $x$-coordinates $x=-2$ and $x=4.$ Given that ${f}^{′}(x)=0$ at both $A$ and $B,$ find the intervals where ${f}^{′}(x)>0.$
feedback.worked_solution:
We have ${f}^{′}(x)=0$ at the critical points $A$ and $B.$ Note the following:

- If $f(x)$ is strictly increasing, then ${f}^{′}(x)>0.$

- If $f(x)$ is strictly decreasing, then ${f}^{′}(x)<0.$

The information about ${f}^{′}(x)$ can be summarized in the following table:

$$
\begin{aligned}x & (-\infty ,-2) & -2 & (-2,4) & 4 & (4,\infty ) \\ f & ↗ & \text{no extr.} & ↗ & \text{max} & ↘ \\ {f}^{′} & + & 0 & + & 0 & -\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, ${f}^{′}(x)>0$ on the intervals $(-\infty ,-2)$ and $(-2,4).$
